finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: Marshal.load on attacker-supplied base64 data in /restore allows remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication

trace.note: Base64.decode64(params[:state]) yields attacker bytes, passed directly to Marshal.load
state.inspect invoked on the deserialized object, which can also trigger gadget methods

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on the state, no class allowlist, no safe alternative such as JSON; Sinatra provides no protection for this. No other files exist in the repo.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 defines an unauthenticated POST /restore route that passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load with no auth, signature, or class allowlist, and app.rb is the only file in the repo.
